subject: Hosted API pricing qualification: monthly tokens & peak TPS
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@finlytics.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — token volumes & cost targets

Thanks again for the time today, Elena — great conversation. As promised, summary and a couple of clarifying questions so we can put together a tight hosted-API estimate and SOW.

Recap of what I heard today:
- Current use case: real-time document summarization + semantic search in the app. Mixed short prompts + long context ingestion (docs).
- Expected production traffic (initial): 150M tokens/month (ingest + generation).
- Peak TPS: ~18 TPS sustained with occasional spikes to 30 TPS during business hours.
- Primary goal: predictable unit economics and predictable latency (~<300ms per response for short prompts).
- Target pricing: customer is evaluating target spend of $800-600 per 1M tokens as a benchmark for vendor selection.

A couple clarifying asks so our pricing calc is accurate:
1) Can you confirm whether the 150M tokens/month is total tokens (input+output) or generation-only?
2) For peak TPS, are the 30 TPS spikes across a single endpoint, or horizontally across multiple endpoints/users?
3) Do you have a procurement/budget window (target PO/signing date)?

Next steps from our side once you confirm: we'll run a cost estimate (hosted API) showing: expected monthly spend at your profile, expected peak concurrency cost impacts, and options to reduce unit cost (responsible batching, prefix caching, short TTL embeddings). I'll attach a first-pass pricing_estimate_v1 and a draft SOW for review.

Thanks —
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.inference | +1 415-555-0123

From: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@finlytics.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — token volumes & cost targets

Hi Ben — thanks for the recap and the doc. Quick answers below: 

1) The 150M tokens is total tokens (input + output). We expect roughly 60% input / 40% output by token count.
2) Spikes to 30 TPS are typically from a single region during peak business hours but distributed across many users hitting the same endpoint. So capacity needs to handle single-endpoint bursts.
3) Procurement timeline: aiming to finalize vendor and have PO by end of October (we have a Q4 budget to spend).

Budget: the team shared an internal target of $750-1,000 per 1M tokens for hosted API given the importance of latency and managed infra. If you can show options to hit the lower end with caching/batching recommendations, that would be helpful.

Elena
Head of Platform | Finlytics
elena.garcia@finlytics.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@finlytics.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — token volumes & cost targets

Thanks Elena — this is super helpful. Based on 150M total tokens / month (60% input, 40% output) and your target $/1M tokens, I ran two quick hosted-API scenarios in the attached pricing_estimate_v1.xlsx:

Scenario A — Standard hosted profile:
- Assumes best-effort batching and default caching
- Unit price: $1,000 per 1M tokens (aligns to mid-point of your target)
- Monthly cost ~= $150,000
- Observed short-prompt latencies in our hosted tier: 150-300ms; longer context ops proportionally higher.

Scenario B — Cost-optimized (recommended for volume):
- Adds prefix KV caching for common doc headers + aggressive batching (workload permitting)
- Quantization-optimized model variant for embeddings & generation where acceptable
- Unit price estimate: $800 per 1M tokens (requires ~30% uplift in allowed latency for heavy gen operations or acceptance of quantized outputs for some routes)
- Monthly cost ~= $120,000

Peak TPS notes:
- With hosted API, 30 TPS spikes are within our multi-tenant headroom, but sustained 30 TPS with low latency SLAs benefits from a dedicated capacity (Reserved/Dedicated) or guaranteed concurrency plan.
- If you require strict <300ms at 30 TPS sustained, we recommend a Dedicated pilot in Q4 as a next step — I can include an option in the SOW.

I've attached the pricing_estimate_v1.xlsx and a draft SOW (SOW_draft_finlytics.pdf). Would you like us to run a brief load-profile test with a simulated 30 TPS spike so we can capture more precise latency-vs-cost numbers? That test would take ~2 business days to run and produce a short report.

If procurement wants an itemized quote or PO-friendly line items, happy to provide. Next milestone: once you confirm Scenario preference (Standard vs Cost-optimized) and whether you want a load test / Dedicated pilot, we'll convert to a formal quote.

Best —
Ben

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@finlytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — token volumes & cost targets

Quick technical note from the SE side:
- 30 TPS spikes across a single endpoint are common; we typically recommend:
  * Prefix caching for doc headers and repeated system prompts (reduces token volume by up to 20-35% for many doc-heavy apps)
  * Batch-window tuning: small batching windows (~20-50ms) preserve latency while increasing throughput efficiency
  * Token-aware routing: route long-context jobs to a separate pool to avoid KV cache thrashing on short requests
- For the load test: we can script a 48-hour window with ramp and 10-minute sustained 30 TPS spike + 1-minute 60 TPS stress bursts to measure tail latency. We'll include recommendations and expected cost delta in the report.

Happy to sync on a short technical call if you want to walk through caching and batching tradeoffs.

— Alex
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

I'll loop in our procurement contact directly (procurement@finlytics.com) for the formal quote. Looking forward to the load-test report and estimated monthly spend at $800/1M tokens.

Best,
Elena
